calls.head: Don’t buy Woll’s slump against the Senators
calls.body: Woll has been shaky against the Senators since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Woll starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .867 against the Senators.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 66% chance, and they delivered.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Philadelphia flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Philadelphia gets outshot more than almost anyone. Not tonight: Philadelphia took 47 of the 81 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Philadelphia would expect about 40%. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.
surprises.flipped: A brick wall against a revolving door

surprises.head: Linus Ullmark stole one
surprises.body: Ullmark allowed 1 goal on 29 shots, worth 3.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than Ottawa’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 25 starts.

story.head: The Senators keep the Flyers winless
paras: The Senators’ William Eklund left in the first period and didn’t return. Nick Cousins opened the scoring for the Senators midway through the period. Matvei Michkov made it 1-1 for Philadelphia on the power play midway through the second, but that’s where Philadelphia’s luck ran out. Carter Yakemchuk put the Sens ahead for good on the power play midway through the third.

The Flyers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Flyers win about six in ten. Linus Ullmark made the difference in net, stopping 28 of 29. Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26 for the Flyers. The Senators moved to 3-1-0. The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-3-2.

items.text: The Senators won their home opener and have beaten the Flyers six straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
The Senators’ Hoyt Stanley played his first NHL game.
Two of the preview’s four calls held.
